label: PF Backlog 591
title: EDP-10: Timeouts, pool budgets, payload/upload limits, per-tenant & global quotas, structured errors; production profile rejects dev/anon auth
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

delivery.note: Gate 0/1.5/1/2.5/2 (APPROVE_WITH_ATTENTION); precheck fast PASS; CI structure PASS

decisions.note: HIL approved Gate 1 ('okay continue') for the 5 decisions: edpsvc target, defaults, in-process quotas, non-superuser runtime DSN, per-tenant attribution + BI-PF-1478.

HIL-approved in the Gate 1 package: graceful drain is 180s (>= 120s upload budget, not 30s); migration DDL timeout is 150s and bypasses the 30s request deadline; /metrics requires the admin token and exposes counters + latency histograms (not counters-only); default global/tenant concurrency is 10/5 to satisfy global<=pool. The design AC text is superseded by this entry.

HIL approved the batch + one final review. Gate 2.5 sha 8f35729011ec: 2 blockers verified false/benign (auditCoverage uses r.Context; BindTenant is transaction-local), 6 majors accepted/deferred (role recheck/ready, tenant attribution -> BI-PF-1478, upload buffering).

brief.problem: edpsvc has no timeouts, body/upload caps, quotas, request ids or structured errors, and opens a DB pool per request; dev/anon auth and a superuser DSN can reach production.
brief.what_adds: Go limits package (env config, request id, timeouts, body/upload caps, tenant+global quotas/concurrency, structured errors) wired into edpsvc; shared bounded pool + graceful shutdown; production profile auth/role guard; GET /admin/limits.
brief.why: Enterprise baseline for performance, safety and least privilege before scale-out.
brief.who_feels: EDP operators, SRE, security reviewers, all edpsvc admin clients.
brief.success: Over-limit/oversize/timeout requests fail predictably in the envelope; production refuses dev/anon auth and a superuser runtime role; tests + precheck pass.

objective: Harden the Go EDP data-plane service with enforceable timeouts, body/upload limits, per-tenant and global quotas/concurrency, a structured error contract, a bounded shared DB pool, and a production profile that fails closed on dev/anon auth or a superuser runtime role.
acceptance_criteria: go/edpsvc enforces configurable request (30s), DB (5s), upload (120s for /artifacts) and server read/write/idle/header timeouts plus a 1 MiB body cap (64 MiB upload cap); over-limit bodies return structured 413, deadlines return 504, and every handler uses r.Context()/dbCtx so cancellation reaches DB/object IO.

A per-tenant and global token-bucket request quota plus per-tenant and global concurrency caps (env-driven, fail-closed) reject over-limit requests with 429 + Retry-After; the tenant key is the tenant the request targets (X-Tenant-Id, validated against the tenant query where present); the global bucket always applies and is the hard anti-evasion control because edpsvc has one admin principal; /health, /ready and /metrics are exempt but still DB-timeout bounded.

Every edpsvc error path returns the versioned envelope {"error":{"code","message","category","retryable","request_id"}} (v1, documented in docs/PF-API-SERVICE-OR-SERVER.md) with X-Request-ID (propagated when valid, else generated); 400/401/403/404/405/409/413/429/500/503/504 map to stable codes and messages are redacted.

PF_PROFILE=production fails closed when PF_DEV/API_ALLOW_ANON/PF_ALLOW_ANON is enabled, PF_ADMIN_TOKEN is missing/default/shorter than 24 chars, or the runtime DB role is superuser/BYPASSRLS; PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0 is refused in production (non-production only), and the superuser escape hatch requires profile != production and PF_ALLOW_SUPERUSER_DSN=1; the error names the offending setting.

edpsvc uses ONE shared bounded store.PgStore for all handlers, validates global concurrency <= PoolOptions.MaxConns at startup, never opens a pool per request, drains in-flight work on graceful shutdown (30s) before closing the pool, and exposes GET /admin/limits (admin) + GET /metrics (counters only: 413/429/504, denials, evictions, pool saturation).

Tests prove: config/validation incl. cap<=MaxConns; token-bucket refill/deny/Retry-After with an injected clock; tenant validation, max-tenant cap (LRU idle eviction, 429 when none idle) and no active-bucket reset; profile/kill-switch/role fail-closed; envelope + request-id propagation + redaction; httptest mux 401/413/429/504; DB-gated shared-pool role guard; go test ./... and precheck pass.
in_scope: go/edpsvc/internal/limits (config, errors, middleware, quota, metrics, profile/role validators, tests)
go/edpsvc/main.go wiring: shared pool, r.Context(), middleware chain, /admin/limits, /metrics, http.Server timeouts, graceful shutdown
Tests: unit + httptest mux + DB-gated role guard
out_of_scope: Shared/distributed quota coordination across replicas (EDP-24 scale-out) and SLO dashboards (EDP-22).
Billing/entitlement semantics and per-tenant quota overrides from the quotas table.
approach: Add go/edpsvc/internal/limits: env Config (defaults/invariants incl. global concurrency <= MaxConns), request-id + v1 error writer, timeout/body-limit/quota/concurrency middleware with per-path timeouts (JSON vs upload), token bucket with injectable clock + idle eviction/max-tenant cap, Prometheus counters, and pure profile/kill-switch/role validators. Refactor edpsvc/main.go to one shared store.OpenWithPool, r.Context()/dbCtx everywhere, GET /admin/limits + GET /metrics, http.Server timeouts and graceful shutdown (drain 30s). Register env flags and document the v1 envelope/routes in docs/PF-API-SERVICE-OR-SERVER.md. PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0 is non-production only. No schema change.

prior_decisions: ADR-0006/ADR-0008: the EDP data-plane service (go/edpsvc) is the Go API surface and the SoR operator; it owns quotas, migrations and admin auth.
BI-PF-1300/BI-PF-1301 (merged): system-of-record schema, tenants/projects and server-side tenant context are available for quota attribution.
BI-PF-1407 (RLS role guard): runtime DB connections must be non-superuser/non-BYPASSRLS; pf_owner is a superuser and bypasses RLS.
EDP-17/BI-PF-1309: go/store exposes PoolOptions (MaxConns, ConnectTimeout) and PgStore.Stats; reuse it rather than a new pool.
EDP-22/BI-PF-1314 owns SLOs/observability/graceful-degradation; BI-PF-0332 owns Python api/ hardening (limits/tenant isolation) - this item covers the Go EDP service only.
existing_path: go/edpsvc/main.go: all handlers; writeJSON success/error helper; adminOnly bearer check; each request calls store.Open (per-request pool) and uses context.Background() in several handlers.
go/store/pool.go: DefaultPoolOptions{MaxConns:10, ConnectTimeout:10s} + OpenWithPool; PgStore.Stats for pool saturation.
go/edpsvc has no timeouts, body limits, quotas, request id or structured error envelope; errors are {"error":"..."}.
api/auth.py + api/errors.py: the Python control-plane auth/error envelope (API_ALLOW_ANON dev flag); separate surface, not the EDP Go service.
config/env-flags.json: central env flag registry (PF_DB_DSN, PF_API_TOKEN, API_ALLOW_ANON).
migrations/0002_core_schema.up.sql: quotas table exists for tenant limits (billing/entitlement overrides out of scope).
assumptions: The EDP-10 target is go/edpsvc (the Go data plane), not the Python api/ surface (BI-PF-0332); 'All HTTP handlers' means every edpsvc route.
Limits are env-configured (exported by the orchestrator) and registered in config/env-flags.json; no new config file/store.
Per-tenant/global request quotas are enforced in-process (token bucket + semaphore); exact multi-replica coordination is EDP-24.
The runtime DSN (PF_DB_DSN) is non-superuser in production; migrations are a deploy step (db_migrate.py); /admin/migrations is dev/ops-only.

Defaults: request 30s, DB 5s, upload 120s, read-header 5s, read 30s, write 180s, idle 120s, max headers/body 1 MiB, upload 64 MiB, pool 10, tenant 600 rpm / 20 concurrent, global 6000 rpm / 100 concurrent; burst = one minute's rate.

edpsvc has ONE admin bearer principal; per-tenant buckets are fair-use attribution for the tenant a request targets, while the global bucket is the hard anti-evasion control. True per-tenant authentication/isolation is the documented auth follow-up (PF-API-SERVICE-OR-SERVER).
Enforcement can be disabled with PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0 ONLY outside production; production refuses that setting at startup.
divergences: Affected files live in go/edpsvc/internal/limits (same module), not a new Go module.
'Config via orchestrator settings' is env vars registered in config/env-flags.json, matching the existing edpsvc path.
The error body changes from {"error":"..."} to the v1 structured envelope (documented breaking shape).
Python api/ hardening is out of scope (BI-PF-0332).

Per-tenant quotas are attribution keyed by the target tenant, not cryptographically bound to a per-tenant principal (edpsvc has one admin principal); the global cap is the security boundary. Confirm or request per-tenant auth as a follow-up.
open_questions: Confirm the target is go/edpsvc (not the Python api/ surface).
Confirm the defaults and the in-process quota model (single-process caps; multi-replica exactness deferred to EDP-24).
Confirm PF_DB_DSN becomes the non-superuser runtime DSN and production migrations run as a deploy step (PF_ALLOW_SUPERUSER_DSN=1 only outside production).
Confirm per-tenant quotas are attribution under the single admin principal (global cap is the hard boundary) OR request per-tenant authentication now (scope increase).
Confirm the new GET /admin/limits + GET /metrics routes and the v1 structured error envelope.

impact_review.evidence: needs_api=true. New admin-only GET /admin/limits + GET /metrics (counters only, no auth like /health); existing routes keep method/path; error body becomes the v1 structured envelope.

evidence: go/edpsvc enforces configurable request, header/read/write and DB timeouts plus a per-request body cap (1 MiB default) and a 64 MiB upload cap on /artifacts; an over-limit body returns the structured 413 envelope, a deadline returns 504, and every handler uses r.Context() so cancellation propagates to DB/object IO.

A per-tenant and global token-bucket request quota plus per-tenant and global concurrency caps (env-driven, fail-closed) reject over-limit requests with 429 and Retry-After; the tenant key is X-Tenant-Id (fallback tenant query), the global bucket always applies, and /health, /ready and /metrics are exempt.

Every edpsvc error path returns {"error":{"code","message","category","retryable","request_id"}} with an X-Request-ID response header; 400/401/403/404/405/409/413/429/500/503/504 map to stable SCREAMING_SNAKE codes and messages are redacted of token/secret material.

PF_PROFILE=production startup fails closed when PF_DEV, API_ALLOW_ANON or PF_ALLOW_ANON is enabled, PF_ADMIN_TOKEN is missing/default/shorter than 24 chars, or the runtime DB role is superuser/BYPASSRLS; the superuser escape hatch is honored only when profile != production and PF_ALLOW_SUPERUSER_DSN=1, and the failure names the offending setting.

edpsvc uses ONE shared, bounded store.PgStore (PoolOptions from env) for all handlers, never opens a pool per request, closes it on graceful shutdown, and GET /admin/limits (admin bearer) returns the effective non-secret limits plus global quota/pool counters.

Tests prove: config parsing/validation; token-bucket refill/deny/Retry-After and concurrency caps; profile + runtime-role fail-closed decisions; the structured envelope and request id; an httptest mux test for 401/413/429/504; a DB-gated test that opens the shared pool and verifies the non-superuser role guard; go test ./... and precheck pass.

impact_review.evidence: New enforcement/error/profile logic is Go in go/edpsvc/internal/limits + edpsvc wiring; env-flags JSON and docs are declarative; language_rule_review BI-PF-1302 = OK (no new shipped Python).
Reuses store.PoolOptions/PgStore/Stats, edpsvc writeJSON, adminOnly and the env config path; no new module, no new table, no duplicate Python auth/error implementation.

Quota key = the tenant the request targets (X-Tenant-Id, validated against the tenant query); edpsvc has one admin principal, so per-tenant buckets are attribution and the global bucket is the hard anti-evasion control; /admin/limits exposes global counters only.
Production profile refuses dev/anon flags, weak/default admin tokens and a superuser/BYPASSRLS runtime role; constant-time token compare; error messages redacted; request ids only.
One shared bounded pool replaces per-request store.Open; server read/write/idle timeouts + graceful shutdown; DB ops use the request/DB deadline.
Admin data-plane surface only; no schema change; the error shape change is documented; enforcement can be disabled with PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0 for rollback.
X-Request-ID + v1 envelope; /metrics exposes 413/429/504, denial, eviction and pool counters; /admin/limits returns the effective limits; EDP-22 consumes them.

verification: go test ./... in go/edpsvc passes: config/strict env, token buckets with injected clock, concurrency/cap/eviction, envelope v1 + redaction, 404/405 fallback, auth-before-quota, body-tenant attribution, chunked 413, mux 504, role/profile guards, and env-flags/code default parity.
DB-gated tests pass with PF_RUNTIME_DSN (pf_app, non-BYPASSRLS): TestCheckDBRoleIntegration and TestReadyWithDB.

Live e2e against pf-pg-test: /health and /ready 200; /admin/limits 401 without a token and 200 with limits/pool/role; per-tenant 200/200/429; body-tenant 200 then 429; chunked 2000B -> 413; unknown path 404 envelope; production+PF_DEV and production+pf_owner exit 1; production+pf_app starts.
go-modules gate: OK (gofmt + vet + build + test); precheck fast is run before the PR.
risks: Error-shape breaking change: documented v1 envelope + stable status codes; enforcement rollback is non-production only.
Per-tenant attribution under one admin principal can be rotated by an authorized admin client: the global bucket is the hard cap; per-tenant auth is a documented follow-up (scope decision requested).
In-process quotas under-enforce across replicas: per-replica fail-closed caps; EDP-24 for shared coordination.
Production DSN guard/staging: PF_ALLOW_SUPERUSER_DSN=1 outside production + clear startup error.
Handlers ignoring r.Context(): convert every DB/object call and add a canceled-context 504 test; a grep guard is not relied on alone.
Quota map growth: idle eviction (10 min) + max-tenant cap; when full with no idle bucket, reject 429 (fail closed) and never evict active buckets.
Upload timeout vs slow links: 120s upload budget distinct from the 30s JSON request budget.
Metrics endpoint exposure: counters only (no tenant/secret data); /metrics is internal like /health.
rollback: Set PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0 to disable quota/timeout/body-limit enforcement (structured errors and the production profile guard remain), or revert the commit; the shared pool and r.Context() changes are behavior-preserving and no schema/data change is involved.
evidence: Candidate core/global_orchestrator.py
Roadmap EDP-10
L1=Go language rule
Design pre-check (BI-PF-1302): answered 10 checklist item(s) before Gate 1.5

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=345a7dc7cb3c
BLOCKER:
  - `PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0` is a fail-open kill switch that contradicts the fail-closed AC for quotas/timeouts; in production it silently removes all limits while /health stays green. Restrict it to profile != production, or drop it.
  - Tenant identity is taken from an unauthenticated `X-Tenant-Id` header, so any client can claim or rotate tenant keys to evade per-tenant quotas and skew concurrency accounting. Bind the tenant key to the authenticated principal.
MAJOR:
  - No stated invariant between global concurrency cap and `PoolOptions.MaxConns`; if cap > pool size, overload converts into request pile-up and 504s. State and test `global_cap <= MaxConns`.
  - A 64 MiB /artifacts upload is often unreachable under the global request/write timeout on slow links; a size cap alone is insufficient — define a per-path upload timeout budget.
  - The error envelope is a wire-breaking change; pin the needs_api/contract decision and versioning in the service contract + GLOSSARY, not just "documented in the service header" (CL-003/CL-001).
  - No metrics for 413/429/504 counts, quota denials, bucket evictions, or pool saturation; /admin/limits counters cannot drive alerting. Emit Prometheus series now even if dashboards are out of scope.
  - Behaviour when the max-tenant cap is reached (reject legitimate new tenants fail-closed vs fail-open) and whether idle eviction can reset an *active* tenant's bucket are unspecified — define and test both.
  - Interaction of `PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0` with the production profile guard is unspecified (does it also bypass the fail-closed startup check?). Must be pinned in the design.
MINOR:
  - Secret redaction needs tests with known token/secret fixtures and a single documented source of truth, else it drifts from the Python redactor.
  - `grep for context.Background` as a test is brittle; prefer a lint rule or an injected-context spy seam.
  - Graceful shutdown: define drain deadline and what happens to in-flight requests when the shared pool closes.
  - /health, /ready, /metrics are exempt from limits but must still carry DB/read timeouts so a hung DB cannot block them unboundedly.
  - Retry-After needs an injectable clock for deterministic tests.
NIT:
  - env-flags.json defaults should be generated from, or asserted against, the Go constants to prevent drift.
  - X-Request-ID: define whether an inbound id is propagated or always regenerated, for trace continuity.
SUMMARY:
  - Design is directionally right (shared pool, r.Context, structured errors, profile fail-closed) but ships a fail-open kill switch and header-derived tenant identity that undermine the core guarantees; both must be resolved before Gate 1.5.
  - Top risks: quota bypass via tenant-key spoofing, concurrency/pool sizing deadlock, and an unversioned breaking error contract.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=ef8643b7f620
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Rollback story conflicts with AC: `PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0` is refused in production, so the stated production rollback (set flag to 0) is impossible; production rollback requires a code revert/redeploy — document this explicitly and define the redeploy rollback runbook + lead time before Gate 1.5.
  - Graceful-shutdown drain (30s) is shorter than the upload budget (120s `/artifacts`) and equal to the 30s JSON request timeout; in-flight uploads will be force-canceled at shutdown. Define shutdown deadline >= max handler budget (or explicitly accept aborted uploads) and test it.
  - Per-tenant attribution from client-supplied `X-Tenant-Id` under a single admin principal is advisory only: any authorized caller can rotate tenant keys to reset per-tenant buckets. Global bucket is the sole real control — state this as a security limitation in `PF-API-SERVICE-OR-SERVER.md` and require the per-tenant-auth follow-up to be tracked with an ID, not just prose.
  - Runtime DB role (superuser/BYPASSRLS) is validated only at startup; a role grant after boot silently violates the fail-closed invariant. Add periodic/on-pool-reconnect revalidation or an explicit documented "startup-only" decision with an alert.
  - Tenant IDs "validated against the tenant query **where present**" leaves unvalidated paths accepting arbitrary bucket keys; unbounded key cardinality is only mitigated by max-tenant cap. Specify exactly which routes perform lookup and fail closed (403/404) on unresolvable tenant, not just cap.
  - Middleware ordering is unspecified: quota must be acquired/released around the whole request (with `defer` release on panic), and 413 body-limit rejections must not permanently consume concurrency slots or unfairly drain tenant tokens. State the chain order and test slot release on panic/cancel.
MINOR:
  - DB 5s deadline vs pool wait: with global concurrency near MaxConns, requests can block in pool acquire beyond 5s; decide whether `dbCtx` covers pool-acquire wait and confirm saturation surfaces as 503/504 rather than hung requests.
  - `/metrics` exposure: "internal like /health" is not an authz control if the port is reachable; require at minimum network binding documentation and no tenant-labeled series (already counters-only) — confirm authn decision explicitly.
  - Observability gap: counters only (413/429/504, denials, evictions, saturation) with no latency histogram per path class (JSON vs upload); diagnosis of timeout regressions will be hard. Add minimal request-duration buckets or state the deferral.
  - Startup validation should also reject obviously inconsistent combos (e.g., request timeout > read/write server timeout, upload cap > 1 MiB default without explicit opt-in) to avoid silent truncation via `http.Server` limits.
  - Redaction rule for messages: define a fixed allowlist of safe message templates rather than ad-hoc redaction, so the "stable code + redacted message" contract is testable and doesn't leak DSN/SQL text.
  - Tests should assert `Retry-After` correctness across bucket refill boundaries with the injected clock, including clock skew, not just a single deny case.
NIT:
  - `X-Request-ID` inbound validation should cap length and charset to prevent log/metrics cardinality abuse; state the regex in the doc.
  - `/admin/limits` response should document whether it exposes tenant-level state (cardinality) or only aggregate counters, to avoid it becoming an enumeration oracle.
  - Env-flag naming consistency: `PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS` vs `PF_ALLOW_SUPERUSER_DSN` prefix conventions should be pinned in `config/env-flags.json` descriptions.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid, well-scoped hardening design with correct language-rule compliance, no schema change, and good fail-closed posture. Top risks: (1) production rollback contradiction with the limits kill-switch, (2) shutdown drain (30s) < upload budget (120s) causing aborted work, and (3) per-tenant quota enforceability under a single admin principal plus startup-only DB-role validation. Resolve these and pin middleware ordering/metrics authz before Gate 1.5.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=a5d63af0cdb7
BLOCKER:
  - `id-blocks.json` gains an unrelated machine-specific entry (`Srinikc-PC5560-28112`) mixed into this PR; unrelated state change must not ship in BI-PF-1302.
  - Chunked-body over-limit returns 400 not 413: `bodyLimitMiddleware` only pre-checks `ContentLength`; for chunked encoding the `*http.MaxBytesError` from `json.Decode`/`ParseMultipartForm` is swallowed by handlers that call `s.bad(w,r,400,…)` instead of inspecting for `MaxBytesError`. AC: "over-limit bodies return structured 413".
  - `s.dbCtx(r)` applies `DBTimeout` (5 s default) to `/admin/migrations/up|down` which previously used `context.Background()`. Long DDL migrations will now be killed after 5 s, breaking the service's own migration path.
  - Error envelope has no explicit `version` field in the wire format; AC requires "versioned envelope (v1)" and only the doc prose mentions v1.
MAJOR:
  - In `Quota.Acquire` the tenant bucket is created (and old buckets evicted) *before* the global token-bucket check; an attacker cycling unique `X-Tenant-Id` values fills/evicts the bucket map without consuming global tokens, weakening the "hard anti-evasion" guarantee the AC depends on.
  - `artifactUpload`'s `ParseMultipartForm` failure always returns 400 "multipart body required" even when the root cause is `*http.MaxBytesError`; should return 413 via `WriteHandlerError`.
  - No test proves that `PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=0` in non-production actually disables the middleware chain (quota/timeout/body-limit) while keeping envelope + profile guard; the AC lists "kill-switch" coverage explicitly.
MINOR:
  - `PF_DEV` and `PF_ALLOW_ANON` are checked in `ValidateProfile` but not registered in `config/env-flags.json`, violating the registry's discoverability contract.
  - `s.fail` logs the raw error unredacted (`log.Printf(... err)`) while the client response is redacted; the log pipeline may capture connection strings or credentials.
  - `statusWriter` does not implement `http.Flusher`; any future streaming handler will silently break.
  - `CheckDBRole` wraps a single SELECT in `WithTx`, adding an unnecessary transaction round-trip per check and per 5-min recheck.
  - `env-flags.json` is wholesale reformatted (compact → expanded) with no functional change for existing entries, creating large merge-conflict surface and review noise.
NIT:
  - `tenantStore(tenant)` ignores its `tenant` argument and always returns `s.st`; the signature is misleading.
  - `artifactSvc` returns a no-op `func() {}` as "close" to preserve an old API shape; the pattern is confusing.
  - `PF_EDP_ADDR`, `PF_MIGRATIONS_DIR`, `PF_OBJECT_BACKEND`, `PF_MEMORY_PRINCIPAL` are used in `main.go` but not registered in `env-flags.json` (pre-existing inconsistency, now more visible).
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=31262631dd48
BLOCKER:
  - Unknown paths fall through to net/http's default plain-text 404 (no `mux.HandleFunc("/", ...)`/NotFoundHandler, and ServeMux's own 405 is unwrapped), so not "every error path" returns the v1 envelope required by AC.
  - Per-tenant quota keys only off `X-Tenant-Id`/`?tenant`; routes whose targeted tenant lives in the JSON body (POST /audit, /jobs, /memory, /backlog) are never attributed to that tenant, so per-tenant rate/concurrency caps don't apply to the tenant actually targeted.
MAJOR:
  - `MigrationTimeout` (10m) exceeds server Read/WriteTimeout (180s) and `Validate()` never cross-checks it: a long DDL migration is killed by `http.Server.WriteTimeout` mid-flight, leaving the client with a reset and the DB work orphaned.
  - AC requires an httptest **mux** 504 test; only a custom-handler 504 test exists (`TestTimeoutWrites504`), so the mux-level deadline path is unproven.
  - `/metrics` has no pool-saturation signal (only `/admin/limits`), and 413/429/504 are merely label values in `edp_http_requests_total`; AC asks for explicit counters, and histograms contradict "counters only".
  - `s.fail` passes `err.Error()` through for status<500, and storage failures are mapped to 400/404 (e.g. `artifactGet` returns 404 + raw message for any `svc.Get` error) → internal/DB details reach clients.
  - "no active-bucket reset" unproven: eviction keys off last token-take only, so a tenant holding concurrency slots across a 120s upload or 10m migration (idle TTL 10m) can have its bucket+semaphore evicted and reset; no test asserts active buckets survive.
  - `metrics.go` hand-rolls a Prometheus renderer under a mutex on every scrape; if the repo already exposes metrics elsewhere this is duplicated infrastructure and a contention/scrape-cost liability.
MINOR:
  - Graceful drain is `max(WriteTimeout,30s)` = 180s by default, not the specified 30s; worse, `st.Close()` runs even when `srv.Shutdown` timed out with handlers still in flight.
  - `/ready` uses a hardcoded 2s ping instead of the configurable `DBTimeout` (AC: exempt routes are "still DB-timeout bounded").
  - `weakTokens` entries are all <24 chars, so the weak-token check is unreachable after the 24-char minimum; a 24-char concatenation of a default token passes.
  - Role-guard/shared-pool integration tests skip without `PF_RUNTIME_DSN`, so the AC's DB-gated guard is unverified in default CI.
  - Whole-file reformat of `config/env-flags.json` destroys blame and risks unrelated golden/diff tests; `Config.AdminTok` is dead; `statusCodes` is a mutable package map.
NIT:
  - Redaction is regex-only; safer posture is to never echo raw `err.Error()` for storage-derived 4xx.
  - Package doc claims `limits` is a leaf depending only on a datastore port, but `profile.go`/tests pull in `productforge/datastore` and `productforge/store` — state the dependency honestly.
  - `statusWriter` implements only `Flush`, not `Hijacker`/`Pusher`/`io.ReaderFrom` — fine today, a trap for future streaming endpoints.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid structural work: single shared pool, structured envelope, fail-closed profile/role checks, injected-clock quota tests, and per-handler DB deadlines all land as intended.
  - Ship-blockers are contract gaps, not plumbing: default 404/405 bypass the v1 envelope, and per-tenant quota ignores body-declared tenants, weakening the tenant attribution AC.
  - Top residual risks: migration vs write-timeout mismatch cutting DDL, internal error text leaking on 4xx paths, and `/metrics` missing the pool-saturation/counter signals ops will need.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=4a66bc50ea3b
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
